topics.title: SyteLine API connection
topics.summary: Connect Enflite automations to Infor CloudSuite SyteLine through ION API: what you need, the steps, and how it works.

blocks.text: Status (2026-10-05, TRN): ION sign-in, the IDO service, and the Mongoose configuration are confirmed on **TRN**. Reading and writing SyteLine data is **not yet confirmed**: it needs credentials with a service account (see [Step 1](/developers/syteline-api-credentials)). This page will be updated once that is tested.

Enflite automations (the **Automation Studio** in the Enflite AI app) read and change **SyteLine** data through Infor's **ION API**. The requests go to SyteLine's own **IDO REST API**, so any IDO a form uses can also be used by an automation. This guide sets up that connection once per environment (**TRN** first, then production).

head: Item
Who provides it
Where it is used
rows: Infor OS admin with the **IONAPI-Administrator** role
The service account runs every request as this user (Step 1)
A `.ionapi` credentials file **with a service account** (`saak` / `sask`)

items: [Create the credentials with a service account](/developers/syteline-api-credentials) in ION API.
[Find the Mongoose configuration](/developers/syteline-api-configuration) for the environment.
[Connect the Enflite backend and test it](/developers/syteline-api-connect) (script, Postman, Studio).
Build automations on [any IDO](/developers/syteline-api-ido), for example [lot tracking at zero on hand](/developers/syteline-api-lot-tracking).
If something fails, see [Troubleshooting](/developers/syteline-api-troubleshooting).
The backend signs in to ION with the `.ionapi` file and gets an OAuth token. With `saak`/`sask` in the file the token carries the service-account user.
It calls SyteLine at `{iu}/{ti}/CSI/IDORequestService/ido/...` with that token and the header `X-Infor-MongooseConfig`.
SyteLine runs the request as that user, with that user's authorization group, and answers `{ Success, Message, ... }`.

blocks.text: Credentials are secrets. Keep the `.ionapi` file in `backend/secrets/` (git-ignored) or the deployment's secret store. Never commit it, paste it in chat, or email it.

topics.subtitle: Infor ION API → SyteLine IDO REST, for Enflite automations

topics.title: Step 1: Credentials with a service account
topics.summary: Create a Backend Service app in ION API and download its .ionapi file with Create Service Account turned on (saak/sask).

blocks.text: Status (2026-10-05, TRN): ION sign-in, the IDO service, and the Mongoose configuration are confirmed on **TRN**. Reading and writing SyteLine data is **not yet confirmed**: it needs credentials with a service account (see [Step 1](/developers/syteline-api-credentials)). This page will be updated once that is tested.

SyteLine runs every API request as a SyteLine user. A `.ionapi` file downloaded **without** a service account only identifies the app, so SyteLine answers every data request with `Invalid token`. The fix is to download the credentials with **Create Service Account** turned on.

items: Pick or create a user for automations, e.g. `svc_enflite_automation`. Use a dedicated user, not a person's account.
In **Infor OS → User Management**, make sure the user exists and has access to SyteLine in this environment (**TRN** first).
In SyteLine, give the user's authorization group what the automations need. For lot tracking: read **Items** and **Item Warehouses** (`SLItems`, `SLItemwhses`) and update **Items** (`SLItems`).
Sign in to the Infor OS portal (Ming.le) for the environment and open **ION API**.
Go to **Authorized Apps** and click **+** (Add).
Set **Type** to **Backend Service**. Name it, e.g. `Enflite Automations TRN`, and add a description.
Click **Save**.
Open the app and click **Download Credentials**.
Turn on **Create Service Account**.
In **User Name**, select the user from 1a.
Click **Download**. Store the file securely: the service-account secret is shown only at download time.

blocks.text: Open the `.ionapi` file in a text editor. It must contain both `saak` and `sask`. If they are missing, it was downloaded without **Create Service Account**: download it again.

head: Field
What it is
Used for
rows: Grant type the app was created with

blocks.text: With `saak`/`sask` the token request is the password grant: `grant_type=password`, `username=saak`, `password=sask`, `client_id=ci`, `client_secret=cs`, posted to `{pu}{ot}`. The Enflite backend does this automatically when the fields are present.

items: [Service Authorized App (.ionapi)](https://docs.infor.com/inforos/latest/en-us/useradminlib_cloud/etl_dl_ag/oda1623328668051.html): Backend Service, **Create Service Account**, select a user, **Download**.

[Registering an authorized app with the Password Credentials grant type](https://docs.infor.com/ln/2026.x/en-us/lnesolh/lnrestapiag/dlr1698245101470.html): the file contains `cn, ci, cs, pu, ot, saak, sask`.

[Infor CloudSuite Industrial (SyteLine) integration guide (MachineMetrics)](https://docs.machinemetrics.com/docs/integrations/erp-connectors/infor-syteline-cloud-connector/): the same setup for SyteLine, from a third party.

topics.title: Step 2: Find the Mongoose configuration
topics.summary: Every SyteLine request through ION needs the X-Infor-MongooseConfig header. Find the configuration name for the environment.

blocks.text: SyteLine needs to know which configuration (site database) to log into. Through ION that is the request header `X-Infor-MongooseConfig`. On CloudSuite the name is usually `<tenant>_Default`.

head: Environment
Configuration
Status
rows: Find it with the steps below

blocks.text: List the configurations in the tenant's group. On CloudSuite the plain list is empty; you must pass `configGroup`.
The Postman request **List Mongoose configurations** does this and fills `mongoose_config` for you.

items: Open SyteLine in the browser for the environment.
Press **F12** to open the developer tools and select the **Network** tab.
Open any form, select a request to the IDO service, and find `X-Infor-MongooseConfig` under **Request Headers**.

topics.title: Step 3: Connect the backend and test
topics.summary: Put the .ionapi file and configuration into the Enflite backend, then test with the script, Postman and the Studio.

blocks.text: Status (2026-10-05, TRN): ION sign-in, the IDO service, and the Mongoose configuration are confirmed on **TRN**. Reading and writing SyteLine data is **not yet confirmed**: it needs credentials with a service account (see [Step 1](/developers/syteline-api-credentials)). This page will be updated once that is tested.

items: Save the `.ionapi` file from Step 1 as `backend/secrets/syteline.ionapi` in `Enflite/backend-ai`. The folder is git-ignored and docker-ignored; only `syteline.ionapi.example` is committed.
In `backend/.env` add `SYTELINE_IONAPI_FILE=/app/secrets/syteline.ionapi` (docker compose) or `SYTELINE_IONAPI_FILE=./secrets/syteline.ionapi` (running natively).
Add `SYTELINE_MONGOOSE_CONFIG=` with the name from [Step 2](/developers/syteline-api-configuration).
Restart the backend: `docker compose restart backend`.

blocks.text: The backend mints and refreshes the token itself, and uses the service account automatically when `saak`/`sask` are in the file. `SYTELINE_BASE_URL` can stay unset; it defaults to `{iu}/{ti}`.
From `backend/` (with docker: `docker compose exec backend` in front). Read-only.

blocks.label: Commands
blocks.code:
npm run syteline:test -- token                     # sign-in works
npm run syteline:test -- probe                     # IDO service reachable
npm run syteline:test -- items --item 91300-017    # item, lot tracked, on hand
npm run syteline:test -- ido SLItems --props Item,Description,LotTracked --where "Item = '91300-017'"

head: Check
Pass looks like
rows: A row with the item, **Lot tracked** and **On hand**; `automation IDO steps → ok`

blocks.text: Import `backend/postman/SyteLine-ION.postman_collection.json` and the example environment, fill the environment from the `.ionapi` file (mark `ci`, `cs`, `sask` as secret), and run:

items: **1. ION sign-in → Get token (service account)**: **Token carries a SyteLine user** must pass.
**2. SyteLine IDO reads**: configurations, **IDO property info (SLItems)**, **Get item**, **Get on hand by warehouse**.
**5. Lot tracking at zero OH**: see [the worked example](/developers/syteline-api-lot-tracking).
In the Enflite AI app open **Studio → Connections** and click **Test** on the `default` connection.
The three IDO actions show as available.
Open **Studio → Templates** to build an automation, or test a single action from **APIs**.

topics.title: Working with any IDO
topics.summary: Read, update and call any SyteLine IDO from an automation: load, update, invoke, filters, row keys and property names.

blocks.text: Automations use SyteLine's IDO REST API, the same API SyteLine's own forms use. Anything a form can read or save through an IDO, an automation can do with the same IDO and property names. The tenant publishes the full reference at `{iu}/{ti}/CSI/IDORequestService/ido/ionapi-doc`.
Actions that change data (**update**, **invoke**) need explicit confirmation when the automation is deployed, are skipped in test runs, and can be placed after an **Approval** step.
Find the IDO and property names

items: In SyteLine open the form, switch to **Design Mode**, and select the field: its **Binding** shows the IDO property; the form's collection shows the IDO (e.g. `SLItems`).
List every property of an IDO with its type and read-only flag: `GET {ido base}/info/{ido}` (Postman **IDO property info**).
Check real values with a load: `npm run syteline:test -- ido <IDO> --props <list> --where "<Property> = '<value>'"`.

blocks.text: These are SyteLine's standard names. Confirm them on your tenant with **IDO property info** before relying on them; custom (UET) fields appear as `Uf_ENF_*` properties.

Use `where` for any value that comes from an input, a webhook or an earlier step. The backend quotes and escapes it (`Item = 'O''Brien'`). Use the raw `filter` only for fixed text you write yourself, e.g. `Stat = 'O'`.

items: **Load** the row first; every row comes back with `_ItemId`, SyteLine's row key.
**Update** with `itemId` = that `_ItemId` (template: `{{steps.<load step>.output.data.Items[0]._ItemId}}`) and only the properties to change.
**Verify** with another load that the value changed.

blocks.label: Update request the backend sends

head: You want
Template / step
rows: A property of the first row
A total (e.g. on hand over all warehouses)

blocks.text: SyteLine can answer HTTP 200 with `"Success": false`. The backend treats that as a failed step (`STUDIO_IDO_FAILED`) and stops the run, so an automation never acts on a failed read.

topics.title: Example: lot tracking when on hand reaches zero
topics.summary: Automatically turn on an item's lot tracking when its on-hand quantity reaches zero, with an approval first.

blocks.text: Status (2026-10-05, TRN): ION sign-in, the IDO service, and the Mongoose configuration are confirmed on **TRN**. Reading and writing SyteLine data is **not yet confirmed**: it needs credentials with a service account (see [Step 1](/developers/syteline-api-credentials)). This page will be updated once that is tested.

**Request:** when an item's on-hand quantity (OH Qty) reaches zero, turn on the item's lot tracking automatically. The Studio template **Enable lot tracking at zero on hand** does this with SyteLine's IDO API.

head: Step
Type
What happens
rows: Checks `SLItemwhses` for the item on a schedule (default every 15 minutes) and runs when its quantities change
`SLItemwhses`: `Item, Whse, QtyOnHand` for the item, all warehouses
A Studio manager approves (expires after 24 hours)
Records the check in the run log

items: Complete Steps 1 to 3 ([credentials](/developers/syteline-api-credentials), [configuration](/developers/syteline-api-configuration), [connect](/developers/syteline-api-connect)) for **TRN**.
In the Enflite AI app open **Studio → Templates → Inventory control → Enable lot tracking at zero on hand** and click **Use template**.
Enter the **Item**, how often to check, and the timezone; pick the connection; click **Create draft**.
On the canvas, click **Test run**. Reads run for real; the approval and the update are skipped and shown as skipped.
Save, then switch **Live** on. Confirm the destructive step when asked (the update changes SyteLine data).
When on hand reaches zero, the run pauses at the approval. A manager opens **Studio → Approvals** and clicks **Approve & resume**; the update and verify run, then the notification.

blocks.text: Folder **5. Lot tracking at zero OH** in the Postman collection runs the same calls in order. Run it with the **Collection Runner**.

items: Pick a **TRN** test item with zero on hand and set `item`.
Run folder 5 with `allow_write` = `false` (dry run). The console shows `DRY RUN: ... would set LotTracked = 1`.
Set `allow_write` = `true` and run again. **LotTracked is now 1** must pass.
Run it a third time: it stops at **already lot tracked**, nothing is written.
It never writes when on hand is above zero or the item is already lot tracked.
The write happens only after an approval, and only in a deployed automation whose destructive step was confirmed.
If SyteLine rejects a read (`Success: false`), the run stops before any write.
Every run is in **Studio → Runs**; the approval decision and the notification are kept.

head: Want
Change
rows: Add `Whse` to the `where` of `onHand` and the trigger
Delete the `review` step (still needs the deploy confirmation)
Use a scheduled trigger and a load without the `Item` filter, or call this automation as a reusable workflow per item

topics.title: Troubleshooting the SyteLine API
topics.summary: Symptoms, causes and fixes for ION sign-in and SyteLine IDO errors.

head: Symptom (exact text)
Cause
Fix
rows: The token has no SyteLine user: the `.ionapi` file has no `saak`/`sask`. Confirmed on TRN 2026-10-05 with the original file, with and without the configuration.
Download the credentials with **Create Service Account** ([Step 1](/developers/syteline-api-credentials)).
Fill them from the new `.ionapi` file
CloudSuite only lists configurations inside the tenant's group
SyteLine answered `Success: false`; the message says why
Read the message: property name, filter, or permission. Check names with **IDO property info**.
The connection was not tested, or the IDO service did not answer
**Studio → Connections → Test**; check `npm run syteline:test -- probe`
That path is the old Enflite REST facade; CloudSuite does not serve it
Load the row first and pass `{{steps.<load>.output.data.Items[0]._ItemId}}`
A Studio manager approves in **Studio → Approvals**
`ci`/`cs` wrong or the app was deleted
